new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Startup Advisory Council was notified in January 2020.
2. Startup India Yatra searches for entrepreneurial talent only in metro cities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Council was notified on 22 January 2020; the Yatra looks for talent in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, not metros.

new.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Platform/Scheme)
A. MAARG
B. Startup India Hub
C. Startup India Yatra
D. SISFS
List-II (Purpose)
1. Single online platform for all stakeholders
2. Mentorship
3. Talent hunt in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities
4. Proof-of-concept funding

new.x: MAARG is the mentorship platform, the Hub is the single online platform, the Yatra hunts talent in smaller cities and SISFS funds proof of concept.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a part of the New Economic Policy of 1991?

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the 1991 reforms:
1. FDI in retail and defence was opened in 1991 itself.
2. Full capital account convertibility was not adopted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: FDI in retail and defence came much later, and the capital account is still only partly convertible.
new.angle: U0515 #19 LPG measures not part (PYQ y1211a84e0c9 angle)

new.s: Which sector remained largely a state monopoly after the 1991 reforms?
new.x: Railways stayed largely a state monopoly, while telecom, banking and civil aviation were opened up.

new.s: Which of the following sectors saw private and foreign entry after the 1991 reforms?
new.x: Telecommunications was reshaped by private and foreign entry; railways, power distribution and ports changed little.

new.s: Which of the following is a measure of privatisation rather than globalisation?
new.x: Disinvestment of PSU equity is privatisation; lower import duties, no import licensing and free FDI are globalisation.

new.s: What happened to the share of agriculture in India's GDP after the 1991 reforms?
o: It first fell and then rose back to its 1991 level
new.x: Agriculture's share fell from about 30% in 1991 to about one-fifth now.

new.s: Which of the following was a usual condition of IMF-World Bank Structural Adjustment Programmes?
new.x: SAP conditions included austerity, privatisation, deregulation, currency devaluation and better tax collection.

new.s: Who was the Finance Minister of India when the 1991 economic reforms were introduced?
new.x: Dr. Manmohan Singh, Finance Minister under P.V. Narasimha Rao, was the architect of the 1991 reforms.

new.s: Who headed the 1991 committee on tax reforms?
new.x: The Raja J. Chelliah Committee (1991) recommended lower tax rates and a wider tax base.

o: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
new.x: About 47 tonnes were pledged by the RBI with the Bank of England (and Bank of Japan); 20 tonnes went via SBI to UBS.
